destinations.name: Hunza Valley
destinations.tagline: Forts, orchards and a ring of 7,000-metre peaks
destinations.description: Karimabad sits on a terrace above the Hunza River, facing Rakaposhi and Diran. Walk the lanes to Baltit and Altit forts, climb to Eagle’s Nest for sunset, and time spring for apricot blossom or late autumn for gold poplars.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: April blossom and late-October colours are the classic windows.
destinations.access: Fly Islamabad → Gilgit (weather-dependent), then about 2 hours by road. By road from Islamabad it is a 1–2 day drive on the Karakoram Highway.
destinations.accessibility: Town base with road access; forts involve stairs and steep lanes.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If it rains: visit Baltit and Altit forts (indoor rooms) and Karimabad's cafés and craft shops; skip high viewpoints.

destinations.name: Skardu & Upper Kachura
destinations.tagline: Glass-still lakes in a cold desert
destinations.description: The capital of Baltistan and the gateway to the Karakoram giants. Row across Upper Kachura’s clear water, stay by Shangrila, explore Shigar Fort and walk the dunes of the Katpana cold desert.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: Summer is green and busy; autumn is calm, clear and cooler.
destinations.access: Fly Islamabad → Skardu (weather-dependent, keep a buffer day). By road it is a long 1–2 day drive via the Karakoram Highway and the Jaglot–Skardu road.
destinations.accessibility: Town base with road and airport access; lake shores are uneven.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If it rains: Shigar Fort and Skardu bazaar; avoid boat rides and the Deosai road.

destinations.name: Attabad Lake
destinations.tagline: Turquoise water born from a mountain
destinations.description: Formed by a landslide in 2010, Attabad is now one of the most vivid lakes in the Karakoram. Take a boat along the cliffs, stop at the lakeside, and continue up the Karakoram Highway into Gojal.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: The colour is brightest on clear summer days.
destinations.access: About 30–45 minutes from Karimabad on the Karakoram Highway, through the lakeside tunnels.
destinations.accessibility: Roadside lake on the KKH; boat rides need a step down onto the boat.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If it rains or the wind is strong: skip the boat ride and stay in Gulmit's village lanes and cafés.

destinations.name: Fairy Meadows
destinations.description: A high meadow facing the Rakhiot face of Nanga Parbat (8,126 m). Reach it by jeep from Raikot Bridge and a short hike, then spend a night under clear skies and walk on to Beyal Camp.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: Snow closes the meadow in winter; June to September is the season.
destinations.access: Jeep from Raikot Bridge on the Karakoram Highway towards Tato, then a 2–3 hour hike. The jeep track is narrow — use local registered drivers.
destinations.accessibility: Jeep track then a 2–3 hour uphill hike; not suitable for wheelchairs or people who cannot hike.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If it rains: stay at the meadow camp and skip the Beyal walk; do not attempt the jeep track during heavy rain.

destinations.name: Deosai National Park
destinations.tagline: The plateau they call the land of giants
destinations.description: One of the highest plateaus in the world, averaging around 4,100 m. Summer turns it into a sea of wildflowers, with Sheosar Lake, marmots and the Himalayan brown bear it protects.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: Open roughly June to September; snow closes it the rest of the year.
destinations.access: Jeep from Skardu via Sadpara Lake, about 2–3 hours to the plateau. Nights are cold even in summer.
destinations.accessibility: High plateau (about 4,100 m) reached by jeep; no facilities; cold nights.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If rain, snow or low cloud: postpone the plateau and use the day in Skardu; the plateau is exposed and cold.

destinations.name: Passu & Gojal
destinations.tagline: Cathedral spires and a swaying bridge
destinations.description: The serrated Passu Cones (Tupopdan, 6,106 m) rise straight above the Karakoram Highway. Cross the Hussaini suspension bridge, walk to Borith Lake and look out over the Passu Glacier.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: Autumn apricot-and-poplar colours make October special.
destinations.access: About 1 hour north of Karimabad on the Karakoram Highway, past Attabad Lake.
destinations.accessibility: Roadside village; the Hussaini bridge is a swaying plank bridge, not suitable for everyone.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If it rains: skip the Hussaini bridge and glacier walk; visit Gulmit's cultural spots instead.

destinations.name: Khunjerab Pass
destinations.tagline: The highest paved border crossing on Earth
destinations.description: At 4,693 m, the top of the Karakoram Highway marks the border with China inside Khunjerab National Park — home to Marco Polo sheep and ibex. Go slowly: the altitude is real.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: Seasonal — typically open late spring to late autumn. Confirm before you go.
destinations.access: A day trip from Passu or Sost along the Karakoram Highway. National park entry is paid at the checkpoint.
destinations.accessibility: Drive-up border pass at about 4,700 m; thin air, keep stops short.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: If snow or storms are forecast: do not drive to the pass; stay lower in Gojal and try another day.

destinations.name: K2 Base Camp & Concordia
destinations.tagline: The throne room of the mountain gods
destinations.description: The great Karakoram trek: walk the Baltoro Glacier past the Trango Towers to Concordia, where K2 (8,611 m), Broad Peak and the Gasherbrums stand in one view. A serious expedition for fit trekkers.
destinations.altitude_note: Approximate elevation of the visited area.

coords.note: Good enough for weather and map links; not for navigation.

destinations.season_note: A short summer window, June to August.
destinations.access: From Skardu by jeep to Askole, then on foot. Requires a trekking permit and a registered operator.
destinations.accessibility: Multi-week glacier trek with permits and an operator; for fit, experienced trekkers only.
destinations.bad_weather_alternative: Weather days are built into expedition plans; follow your licensed operator and guide.

season_notes.winter: Deep winter. High plateaus, passes and treks are usually closed by snow. Skardu and Hunza towns usually stay reachable, but flights are weather-dependent and the KKH can close after heavy snowfall.
season_notes.spring: Blossom season. Apricot and cherry trees flower in Hunza and Skardu while high routes are still thawing and often closed.
season_notes.summer: Peak season. High routes such as Deosai, Fairy Meadows, Khunjerab and the Baltoro are usually open, but monsoon rain can bring landslides: check road status before you travel and book stays early.
season_notes.autumn: Golden season. Poplars and orchards turn gold, skies are often clear and crowds thin out. High routes begin closing from late autumn.
